main_text.head: De cerebro, adipe, offium medul-la, sanguine;
main_text.p: EX medullarum genere exiftere cete-brum Galenus 2: de temperamentis, & 2. de vsu part. scripsit; Gujus quoque sententiæ videtur fuisse Plato in Timæo, ubi medullæ morbum omnium periculosissi-mum esse scriptum reliquit, sub medullæ nomine cerebrum intelligens; non spina-lem medullam, ut aliqui putant, vel alias me-dullas, quod verba Platonis ostendunt. Vide Mercurial. variar. lect.[?] lib. 1. c. 9. Caeterum ce-rebra animalium, tempore Plutarchi man-ducati cæpisse; quæ tamen antiquitas abo-minata projecerit, idem affirmat 8. symp. probl. 9. Hodie inter præcipuas epulas quædam re-poni video, præcipuè verò vitulorum, hœ-dorum, leporum, suum; quin & atiùm mul-tarum atq; piscium. Inter damnatos autem cibos à grauibus autoribus cerebra colloca-ri reperio, ob naturam pituitosiorem, diffi-cilemque concoctionem, tum etiam, quod stomacho adversentur, fastidiumq; afferant. Unde Galenus postremo cibo cerebrum pinguiter conditum vomitu indigentibus exhibendum suadet, sic enim faciliorem fo-re vomitionem. Coquuntur multis modis, elixantur interdum, quandoq; friguntur, vel carbonibus assatur[?]. Suillum marasmo ta-bescen-

page.notes: Uncertain readings: "lect." (the abbreviation after "variar." may be read differently) and "assatur" are marked [?]. "pituitosiorem" is a plausible reading of a word partly obscured by the page curve. The heading's hyphenated "medul-la" and the page-ending "bescen-" follow the printed line breaks. The page is slightly skewed at the bottom edge, and the last line is only partly legible, so "bescen-" may be incomplete.
